title: "New design conference Vectors sold out in 2 days for a great reason"

category: "design"

There’s a hot new tech design conference in town — [Vectors](https://2017.sfdesignweek.org/events/vectors-conference/) — and it sold out in two days flat. I know what you’re thinking — the last thing San Francisco needs is another room full of badge wearing, Mac-toting nerds listening to “thought leaders” wax eloquent.

But Vectors is a far cry from the usual fodder. Its talks aren’t about [“strategic hashtag design”](https://schedule.sxsw.com/2014/events/event_IAP20030) or [“content and commerce”](https://schedule.sxsw.com/2014/events/event_IAP18788) — they’re on channeling vulnerability and designing for unconscious bias. Its speakers aren’t the typical tech bro crowd either.

At its heart, this is a conference about divergent perspectives, and there’s clearly a hunger for it. People bought 300 tickets, and another 150 hopefuls are standing by on the guest list.

![](data:image/png;base64,)![](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/599r6htc/regionalized/17a007a72e60262796bfca57adbed5c43c8f39b5-1600x732.png?rect=1,0,1599,732&w=804&h=368&q=75&fit=max&auto=format)

[Figma](https://www.figma.com/) believes in the mission of the Vectors (we’re sponsoring it) so we sat down with one of the organizers, Facebook designer [Gabe Valdivia](https://twitter.com/gabrielvaldivia), to get more details.

![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)![](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/599r6htc/regionalized/61807420363e845b6fec852d1520a644bd00a6ea-262x261.jpg?w=262&h=261&q=75&fit=max&auto=format)

Carmel D.

**So, how did Vectors come about?**

![](data:image/png;base64,)![](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/599r6htc/regionalized/a89afe5597ec300eb0e8e345cc6ffb0112c42b76-399x399.png?w=399&h=399&q=75&fit=max&auto=format)

Gabriel V.

This idea started after a conversation I had with Julio Martinez, a board member at AIGA and one of the people now organizing Vectors with me. He’s of Mexican descent, I’m Cuban, and we feel a responsibility to contribute to the conversation around diversity.

I never considered my Hispanic heritage much — I’m one of the most whitewashed Hispanics out there. But in some ways I’m in this position where my background represents me and vice versa.

![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)![](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/599r6htc/regionalized/61807420363e845b6fec852d1520a644bd00a6ea-262x261.jpg?w=262&h=261&q=75&fit=max&auto=format)

Carmel D.

**I heard that diversity was your angle, but I didn’t see that actual word anywhere on your site.**

![](data:image/png;base64,)![](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/599r6htc/regionalized/a89afe5597ec300eb0e8e345cc6ffb0112c42b76-399x399.png?w=399&h=399&q=75&fit=max&auto=format)

Gabriel V.

Yeah and that’s intentional. Companies usually have a diversity initiative and it’s composed of African Americans and women or minorities. That’s good to give people a voice, but it winds up being stuck between those who self select. I’d like as many white males in the \[Vectors\] audience who don’t care about diversity as possible so they have a revelation.

![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)![](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/599r6htc/regionalized/61807420363e845b6fec852d1520a644bd00a6ea-262x261.jpg?w=262&h=261&q=75&fit=max&auto=format)

Carmel D.

**What kind of ‘revelation’?**

![](data:image/png;base64,)![](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/599r6htc/regionalized/a89afe5597ec300eb0e8e345cc6ffb0112c42b76-399x399.png?w=399&h=399&q=75&fit=max&auto=format)

Gabriel V.

In the specific case of a white male, it’s how to use their privilege to invite different perspectives and to understand with a high degree of detail what the value of a different perspective is.

I firmly believe if you’re a minority in tech you have a huge advantage and I’ve used that advantage in the past.

![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)![](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/599r6htc/regionalized/61807420363e845b6fec852d1520a644bd00a6ea-262x261.jpg?w=262&h=261&q=75&fit=max&auto=format)

Carmel D.

**Really? Wouldn’t many people say that being a minority in tech is a disadvantage because of discrimination?**

![](data:image/png;base64,)![](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/599r6htc/regionalized/a89afe5597ec300eb0e8e345cc6ffb0112c42b76-399x399.png?w=399&h=399&q=75&fit=max&auto=format)

Gabriel V.

A lot of times people in positions of power in the industry don’t have the experiences we do. I’ve had really bad jobs — \[inaudible\], I’ve worked as a waiter, I’ve worked at a call center being cussed out. That’s revealed resilience in me that a lot of minorities have, because we have to endure things other people don’t.

![](data:image/png;base64,)![](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/599r6htc/regionalized/bc19c57c40f9540675d129b80754c9e1ca15045f-1400x933.png?w=804&h=536&q=75&fit=max&auto=format)

![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)![](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/599r6htc/regionalized/61807420363e845b6fec852d1520a644bd00a6ea-262x261.jpg?w=262&h=261&q=75&fit=max&auto=format)

Carmel D.

**I wasn’t able to hear the first job you mentioned, what was it again?**

![](data:image/png;base64,)![](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/599r6htc/regionalized/a89afe5597ec300eb0e8e345cc6ffb0112c42b76-399x399.png?w=399&h=399&q=75&fit=max&auto=format)

Gabriel V.

Cleaning car dealerships. When we first moved from Costa Rica to the US, my parents, brother and I would go to car dealerships and clean them to make rent. We were literally the people who clean the floors and the trash cans — that was me not that long ago. A lot of Hispanics I know do whatever they need to do to pay rent.

![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)![](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/599r6htc/regionalized/61807420363e845b6fec852d1520a644bd00a6ea-262x261.jpg?w=262&h=261&q=75&fit=max&auto=format)

Carmel D.

**How does coming from that perspective change the way you design?**

![](data:image/png;base64,)![](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/599r6htc/regionalized/a89afe5597ec300eb0e8e345cc6ffb0112c42b76-399x399.png?w=399&h=399&q=75&fit=max&auto=format)

Gabriel V.

Everything you make has a little bit of you in it. Most products have a lot of white male in it — which is fine, that perspective is important — but it means there’s other perspectives just waiting to be exposed.

![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)![](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/599r6htc/regionalized/61807420363e845b6fec852d1520a644bd00a6ea-262x261.jpg?w=262&h=261&q=75&fit=max&auto=format)

Carmel D.

**Can you give me an example?**

![](data:image/png;base64,)![](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/599r6htc/regionalized/a89afe5597ec300eb0e8e345cc6ffb0112c42b76-399x399.png?w=399&h=399&q=75&fit=max&auto=format)

Gabriel V.

Before Facebook, I worked at a startup called Automatic, doing the marketing and video announcing the product. One of the things I was able to do easily was add Spanish subtitles to the video, so Spanish-speaking markets could understand it. Those tiny details add up to a lot of value.

![](data:image/png;base64,)![](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/599r6htc/regionalized/a67ecf20d9495231c490c66c584f87bf306b1166-1230x742.png?w=804&h=485&q=75&fit=max&auto=format)

![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)![](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/599r6htc/regionalized/61807420363e845b6fec852d1520a644bd00a6ea-262x261.jpg?w=262&h=261&q=75&fit=max&auto=format)

Carmel D.

**To bring it back to Vectors, which speaker are you most excited about?**

![](data:image/png;base64,)![](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/599r6htc/regionalized/a89afe5597ec300eb0e8e345cc6ffb0112c42b76-399x399.png?w=399&h=399&q=75&fit=max&auto=format)

Gabriel V.

I was intimately involved in choosing the speakers, that’s like choosing your favorite son! I’ll be moderating one of the panels that has three speakers, can I choose that one?

![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)![](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/599r6htc/regionalized/61807420363e845b6fec852d1520a644bd00a6ea-262x261.jpg?w=262&h=261&q=75&fit=max&auto=format)

Carmel D.

**So you’re choosing yourself.**

![](data:image/png;base64,)![](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/599r6htc/regionalized/a89afe5597ec300eb0e8e345cc6ffb0112c42b76-399x399.png?w=399&h=399&q=75&fit=max&auto=format)

Gabriel V.

Exactly. Blame it on my ego.

In all seriousness though, [Robyn Kanner](https://twitter.com/robynkanner) is a speaker I’m really excited about. I haven’t met her yet but she’s a transgender designer. That’s not a perspective I would’ve sought if I continued to equate diversity with brown people.

My colleague from Facebook, [Michelle Morrison](https://twitter.com/michelephant), helped expand our definition of diversity when she joined us as an organizer.

![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)![](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/599r6htc/regionalized/61807420363e845b6fec852d1520a644bd00a6ea-262x261.jpg?w=262&h=261&q=75&fit=max&auto=format)

Carmel D.

**You sold out super fast, so what do you say to the unlucky souls who didn’t get a ticket?**

The livestream will be on Google Design’s YouTube channel, and we’re organizing watch parties on Spectrum, a website for communities to interact together. Everyone who’s interested can join our Spectrum community not just for a dialogue during the event, but also for a connection beyond the conference.
